response.sql: WITH race_pts AS (SELECT raceId, AVG(points) AS race_avg, COUNT(*) AS result_count FROM constructorResults WHERE points >= 1.0 GROUP BY raceId), race_name_avg AS (SELECT r.name, AVG(rp.race_avg) AS name_avg FROM races r JOIN race_pts rp ON rp.raceId = r.raceId GROUP BY r.name), scored AS (SELECT r.raceId, r.name, rp.race_avg, rp.result_count, rp.race_avg / rna.name_avg AS ratio FROM races r LEFT JOIN race_pts rp ON rp.raceId = r.raceId LEFT JOIN race_name_avg rna ON rna.name = r.name) SELECT raceId, name, race_avg, result_count, ratio FROM scored ORDER BY ratio IS NULL, ratio DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each row in constructorResults is one constructor's result in one race, so the per-race average and count are taken over those rows. The schema does not enforce uniqueness on (raceId, constructorId), so duplicate rows would be counted.

Races with no constructor results of at least 1.0 points are kept with NULL average, count, and ratio, so that 'missing ratios last' applies. They are excluded from the race-name averages, since AVG over their NULL per-race averages has nothing to average.
'Race name' means races.name, and races sharing a name are grouped across all years and rounds, as the request says.
